steps.description: Fit the within-subject differential expression model on the raw integer counts. Pre-filter minimally: keep a gene with at least 10 counts in at least 5 samples (the smallest group size). Build the DESeqDataSet with design ~ subject + condition, setting the condition reference level EXPLICITLY to the control level as named in metadata.csv (do not rely on alphabetical order), and set subject as a factor. Let DESeq2 estimate median-of-ratios size factors inside the model — pass the counts unmodified, with no length correction, no CPM/TPM conversion and no tximport, since these are already gene-level featureCounts values. Run the Wald test and extract the condition treated-vs-control contrast with alpha = 0.05, independent filtering on, BH adjustment. Inspect and save the histogram of unadjusted p-values before reading the adjusted values, and state its shape. Apply apeglm shrinkage to the condition coefficient for reporting and ranking, keeping both the unshrunken log2FoldChange with its lfcSE and the shrunken value in the output table. Report separately the number of genes with NA p-values from the Cook's-distance outlier flag (with 5 replicates per cell DESeq2 flags rather than replaces) and from independent filtering. Also run the GC-content and gene-length bias diagnostic: plot the log ratio of each sample's counts against the median sample versus gene length and versus GC content, and report whether a trend exists. Write the full results table (gene symbol, baseMean, log2FoldChange, lfcSE, shrunken LFC, stat, pvalue, padj) and the significant subset at padj < 0.05.

steps.description: Take the T1S2 results and the filtered count matrix and answer the per-subject part of the research question directly. First, compute for every significant gene (padj<0.05) the within-pair log2 ratio treated/control in each of the 5 subjects from the size-factor-normalized counts, and tabulate it as a genes-by-subject matrix; report per gene how many of the 5 subjects move in the same direction as the fitted effect, and draw a heatmap of the per-subject log2 ratios for the top genes ranked by the apeglm-shrunken log2 fold change. Flag genes whose group-level call rests on one or two subjects. Second, run an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test on the same filtered counts with the same design ~ subject + condition and TMM normalization, at BH padj<0.05; report the number of significant genes from DESeq2, from edgeR, and the size of the intersection, present the intersection as the high-confidence set and the method-specific genes as a secondary set naming the method. Third, assemble the report: MA plot and dispersion plot from the DESeq2 fit placed before the gene tables, the p-value histogram, the design formula, the contrast, the thresholds, the number of genes tested after filtering, the number of DE genes, package versions, and sessionInfo.

plan.title: Paired treated vs control DE in 5 subjects
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a single gene-level raw integer count matrix from STAR/featureCounts (/eval-four-models-with-paired-n5-1/data/inputs/counts/counts.csv, 12000 genes x 10 sample columns plus the gene-symbol first column) with a 10-row sample table (/eval-four-models-with-paired-n5-1/data/inputs/metadata/metadata.csv: sample, subject, condition). Five human blood subjects each contribute one control and one treated sample, so the design is a complete, balanced paired design with n=5 pairs. The research question — which genes respond to treatment within each subject — is answered by a within-subject contrast: DESeq2 with design ~ subject + condition, where the subject term absorbs between-subject variation so the condition coefficient is the paired treated-vs-control effect (knowledge rule R-0011). T1S1 runs the sample-structure QC first (blind VST, PCA on the 500 most variable genes, sample-distance heatmap, library sizes), coloured by condition and by subject, because in a paired design the dominant axis of variance is usually the subject and that must be seen before the model is fitted; it also confirms the 5x2 pairing in the metadata and flags any sample that breaks its pair. T1S2 fits the model: minimal pre-filter (>=10 counts in at least 5 samples, the smallest group size), median-of-ratios size factors estimated inside the model on unmodified integer counts (no length correction, no tximport — the counts are already gene-level featureCounts output), Wald test on the condition coefficient with the control level set explicitly as the reference, apeglm shrinkage for reporting and ranking, and BH adjustment at alpha 0.05 with independent filtering on. Because the counts come from an aligner plus a counter rather than a bias-aware quantifier, the step also runs the GC/length bias diagnostic (log count ratio against the median sample versus gene length and GC content) and reports the trend; cqn and EDASeq are not installed, so if a trend appears the step reports it as a limitation rather than correcting it. With 5 replicates per cell, DESeq2 flags rather than replaces Cook's-distance count outliers and sets those p-values to NA, so the step reports NA counts by cause. T1S3 adds a per-subject view that the group-level table cannot give: the within-pair log2 ratio of each significant gene in each of the five subjects, so a gene driven by one subject is distinguishable from one that moves consistently in all five, plus an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit with the same ~subject+condition design as an independent second method, reporting the intersection as the high-confidence set. Scope is deliberately limited to differential expression — the question asks which genes respond, not which pathways, so no enrichment step is planned. n=5 pairs is modest; the report must state the number of tested genes, the number of DE genes, and that a null result is not evidence of no effect.

Keep genes with >=10 counts in at least 5 samples
